text: I'm doing a systematic review on digital peer support interventions for family caregivers of people with dementia. Database searches (Scopus, Web of Science, PubMed) gave about 1,900 records and I have to screen titles and abstracts before full text. I tried Rayyan but I want something I can drive entirely from the keyboard and that shows the inclusion terms in the abstract so I can decide fast. One record at a time: title, authors, venue, year, abstract. Include / exclude / maybe on i, e and m. If I exclude I have to pick a reason from our protocol list (wrong population, not dementia, no peer support component, not digital/online, wrong publication type, conference abstract only). Show how far through I am and the counts I'll need for the PRISMA flow diagram. Make up 15 or so records for now, I'll paste the real export in after.
pressing e jumped straight to the next abstract before I could pick a reason. e should open the reasons and then 1-6 picks one, so I never touch the mouse. esc to back out if I hit e by mistake

the scopus and wos exports overlap so the same paper shows up twice (sometimes different capitalisation or a full stop at the end). drop duplicates by title before the queue, ignoring case and punctuation, and count them, PRISMA needs the number removed

half the UK papers say carer not caregiver so they dont light up. let me edit the keyword list myself. and can words like protocol, review, children be flagged differently? those are usually excludes but I still want to read them

need an export. csv, one row per record with my decision, the reason, a note and when. my second screener is doing her own pass in her copy and we'll compute kappa in R, so put screener initials in the file and the filename. keep the duplicates in as rows too so both files line up
done with the first pass. how do i go back through just the maybes? add a queue filter: all / not screened / maybes. also a key to jump to the next one I haven't screened
